messages:
maria: quick RFC follow-up — thinking about consolidating per-customer artifact repos into a compact, merged index for on‑prem installs. goal: cut on-disk footprint and simplify delta delivery for air‑gapped customers. tradeoffs i see: operator UX (preflight failures become higher-stakes), signature surface area, and rollback anchors. thoughts?

kevin: +1 on footprint wins. main worry is verification boundary: if we merge indexes we need clear manifest-level sigs so a verifier can assert compatibility without fetching large blobs. otherwise we end up with a TOCTOU window. :eyes:

sophia: agree re: UX. we should produce a deterministic preflight artifact that operators can run locally before activation. e.g., `preflight.json` that lists missing blobs, hash mismatches, and activation safety flags. then console can render a single failure reason instead of raw stack traces.

adam: can we avoid full-merge by doing a hybrid: merged index for metadata + per-component content pointers? merged index speeds delta computation but keeps blobs sharded by original component so rollback is simpler. we should also keep a stable activation anchor (a small signed marker file) that operators can pin to for rollback.

anna: rollout ops question — how do we canary this without a full repo migration? can we serve both indexes in parallel and route a fraction of cluster pulls to the merged index? Also, does dedupe change? if merged index dedupes across components, offline seed caches might shrink unpredictably.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary registry proxy started for staging-1 -> merged-index; tracing id=deploy-6543

kevin: about canaries — yes run dual-index mode. plan: proxy responds to `X-Index-Version` header; default still per-component. start with 5% traffic to merged. add a strict preflight gate that fails activation if the preflight artifact reports any unknown missing blobs.

ops-bot: ops-bot: preflight job queued for staging-1 (job=pf-789). will upload `preflight.json` to /var/log/preflight/staging-1/ once complete.

sophia: sample manifest suggestion for merged index (very small):

```
{
  "index_version": 2,
  "components": [
    {"name":"runtime","digest":"sha256:aaa...","blobs":["b1","b2"]},
    {"name":"models","digest":"sha256:bbb...","blobs":["b2","b3"]}
  ],
  "activation_anchor": {"seq": 134, "signed_by":"sig-v2"}
}
```

adam: we should include compatibility tags: `min_operator_version` and `recovery_anchor` (points to previous anchored seq). if activation fails, operator can attempt `recovery_anchor` which is a lightweight metadata-only swap back.

maria: this is helpful. proposed next steps: 1) spec merged-index format (kevin + sophia) 2) preflight tool prototype that emits `preflight.json` and exit codes (sophia + ops) 3) proxy dual-index routing and `X-Index-Version` header (adam) 4) rollout plan doc with canary percentages + metrics (maria + anna). i'll own the rollout doc and collect canary telemetry keys. anyone want to take ownership of the rollback anchor story? @kevin?

kevin: i can own rollback anchor story. will sketch acceptance criteria: deterministic anchor creation, small size (<4KB), signed with rotating key, and stored in both index variants.

anna: I'll draft the canary playbook and include metrics: preflight-fail-rate, activation-fallback-rate, median activation time. also add an operator-runbook section for manual preflight replay.

maria: thanks — i'll put a bones RFC doc in the rfc tracker and link it here when ready. also — small ask: keep the preflight format stable (v1) even if internals change. ops tooling depends on it.

kevin: ack.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: automated test run completed for merged-index proto (all unit tests passed).

maria: awesome. closing loop for now — expect RFC link later today. :thumbsup:
